ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: ab is a closed rectangular conducting coil that can rotate around an axis O perpendicular to the plane of the paper. During the process in which the slider P of the sliding rheostat R slides from left to right, how will coil ab rotate?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a fixed wound coil on each of the left and right sides. They form the same external circuit with the power supply labeled "power supply" below, the sliding rheostat R, and the slider P. In the middle there is an inclined closed rectangular conducting coil, labeled a and b, and it can rotate around the O axis perpendicular to the plane of the paper; the O axis is near the middle of the small coil. The slider P of the sliding rheostat is drawn above R and connected to the left-side wire, and the right end is connected toward the power supply, so when the slider moves from left to right, the effective resistance connected into the circuit decreases. Reasoning: P slides to the right, the resistance connected into the circuit by the sliding rheostat decreases, and the current in the fixed coils increases, so the magnetic field produced by the left and right fixed coils in the middle region strengthens. According to the winding direction of the fixed coils in the figure and the right-hand screw rule, the direction of the magnetic field in the middle can be determined; because this magnetic flux is increasing, an induced current is produced in the closed coil ab. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should hinder the strengthening of the original magnetic field. After thereby determining the induced current directions in the two effective sides of coil ab, put them back into the original magnetic field and use the left-hand rule to judge the directions of the Ampere forces: side a is subjected to a force upward, and side b is subjected to a force downward. Side a is on the lower-left side of the O axis and is subjected to an upward force, and side b is on the upper-right side of the O axis and is subjected to a downward force. These two forces produce torques in the same direction about the O axis, and the direction is clockwise. Final answer: coil ab will rotate clockwise.
